question: What main type of information is gathered when taking a health history from a patient?
explanation: Subjective data is information the patient or caregiver tells you directly, which forms the core of any health history. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is taking a detailed patient history so important in nursing?

options.A: It serves primarily as a legal document for hospital billing
options.B: It guides clinical reasoning and shapes the nursing care plan
options.C: It eliminates all risks of medication administration errors
options.D: It replaces the need for physical examinations entirely

explanation: A thorough history gives you the vital clues needed to make good clinical decisions and plan the right care for your patient. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which type of question helps a patient talk freely about their symptoms in their own words?
explanation: Open-ended questions encourage patients to share more details, giving you a clearer picture of what they are experiencing. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: A newly admitted patient looks anxious and avoids eye contact. What should you do first?

options.A: Establish a calm, welcoming environment and use gentle non-verbal cues
options.B: Demand that the patient look up when speaking to clinical staff
options.C: Document that the patient is uncooperative and leave the bedside
options.D: Ask family members to answer all questions to speed up the process

explanation: Creating a safe and friendly space helps lower the patient's anxiety so they can trust you before you ask personal health questions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of biographical data collected during a health history?
explanation: Biographical data covers basic background details like age, gender, and job, which help you understand their daily life and health risks. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main reason for asking about a patient's family medical history?

options.A: To predict the exact date of discharge based on relative recovery times
options.B: To identify inherited risks for chronic conditions like hypertension or diabetes
options.C: To determine the financial status of the extended family members
options.D: To trace the legal lineage of the patient for hospital inheritance claims

explanation: Family history reveals genetic health patterns that might put the patient at risk for certain long-term illnesses. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: In the PQRST pain assessment tool, what does the letter 'P' stand for?
explanation: The 'P' helps you find out what makes the pain worse or what makes it feel better. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient says a sharp chest pain started ten minutes ago while resting. Which part of the PQRST framework is this?
explanation: When pain starts, how long it lasts, and how often it happens all fall under the timing category. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which part of the health history covers past hospital stays and major injuries?
explanation: This section records all major illnesses, surgeries, injuries, and past hospital admissions a patient has experienced. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important to know a patient's past surgical history before they undergo a new procedure?

options.A: To verify the exact hospital where the previous doctor trained
options.B: To update the patient's employment status in the hospital system
options.C: To identify prior reactions to anesthesia and surgical complications
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of past healthcare visits

explanation: Knowing how a patient reacted to past surgeries or anesthesia helps the medical team keep them safe during new procedures. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: What kind of information do you gather during a review of systems?

options.A: Surgical consent forms signed by relatives
options.B: Objective physical examination measurements and lab results
options.C: Direct observations made under a microscope
options.D: Patient-reported symptoms across various body systems

explanation: The review of systems is a checklist of symptoms the patient reports, moving step-by-step through different body parts. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of doing a review of systems during an interview?

options.A: It serves as a legally binding contract for surgical intervention
options.B: It replaces the need to check vital signs or physical reflexes
options.C: It diagnoses the exact pathology without requiring laboratory tests
options.D: It uncovers symptoms the patient forgot to mention during the chief complaint

explanation: Going through body systems step-by-step helps catch small or forgotten details that are important for the patient's health. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is looked at during a lifestyle and psychosocial assessment?

options.B: Exact microscopic cell count in the blood
options.C: Use of alcohol, tobacco, or traditional remedies

explanation: This assessment checks daily habits and substance use that can affect the patient's health or treatment. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why should nurses ask patients if they use traditional remedies?

options.A: To replace all modern nursing interventions with local herbs
options.B: To report illegal practitioners to local law enforcement agencies
options.C: To check for potential interactions with prescribed orthodox medications
options.D: To determine the financial budget of the patient's household

explanation: Many people use local herbs alongside hospital drugs, and checking for bad drug interactions keeps the patient safe. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h7)

question: In the eyes of the law, what happens if a nursing assessment is not written down?

options.A: It is legally considered not done
options.B: It is assumed to be completed verbally
options.C: It is automatically updated by hospital management
options.D: It is classified as private personal property

explanation: If it is not documented in the patient's records, legally it is treated as though it never happened. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h8)

question: What should you avoid doing when writing down patient history findings?

options.B: Using judgmental language or personal opinions
options.C: Recording subjective data in direct quotes
options.D: Writing entries promptly after the interview

explanation: Nursing documentation must stay strictly professional, factual, and free of personal bias or emotional comments. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h8)
